newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi non-committal on press report of Kohl meeting.
newsitem.headline: Prodi non-committal on press report of Kohl meeting.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi gave a non-committal response on Friday to a newspaper report that he would meet German Chancellor Helmut Kohl for talks on Italy's bid to join a single European Union currency.
The Milan financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said Prodi would try to overcome German reluctance to see Italy participate in the single currency in a first wave of members from the start of 1999.
Asked about the report, Prodi told a news conference: "I read in the newspapers that we will be seeing Kohl."
It gave no date for the planned meeting but Corriere della Sera newasper said the two leaders could hold talks as early as next week.

Il Sole 24 Ore said the meeting was also intended to resolve tensions which had been fuelled by recent remarks by Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini. An official Italian sources said that element of the report was "devoid of foundation".

Dini's comments have led to speculation that Italy could veto either an intergovernmental conference on reforming European Union institutions or enlargement of the EU unless it is admitted to European economic and monetary union (EMU).

The row between the German government and the Bundesbank over a plan by Finance Minister Theo Waigel to revalue gold reserves and transfer part of the gains to Bonn is seen as strengthening Italy's own case for being allowed into EMU.
Italy, which has been accused of resorting to creative accounting to help wrestle down a public sector deficit, could now level the same charge at Germany, analysts say.
The Bundesbank has said the gold revaluation plan could endanger the future stability of a single currency.
Prodi declined to comment on the Bundesbank position.
"I've been busying myself with Italian difficulties. I am not saying anything about Germany's," he said.
He was speaking after the Italian cabinet approved economic forecasts for the years 1998-2000 which Prodi said would ensure that Italy would be ready for EMU with its "cards in order".
